newsitem.title: ITALY: Italian PM urges clemency for U.S. death row man.
newsitem.headline: Italian PM urges clemency for U.S. death row man.

text.p: Prime Minister Romano Prodi and Italian anti-death penalty activists appealed on Saturday for clemency for U.S. death row inmate Joseph O'Dell, who is due to be executed next week.

Italy, which has no death penalty in civilian criminal cases, is among the most vociferous advocates of a worldwide abolition of capital punishment and Italians have staged street protests to call for clemency for O'Dell.

"Allow me to express my deepest concern and that of the Italian people and humanitarian organisations over the planned execution of O'Dell," Prodi said in a message to George Allen, governor of Virginia.

"Without any intention to interfere with the application of the law in your state and with respect (for)...Virginia's legal system, I appeal for clemency and ask you to consider suspending the execution," he said.

O'Dell is sentenced to die on July 23 following a decision last month by the U.S. Supreme Court to uphold a death sentence imposed in 1986 when he was found guilty of killing a woman. He denies committing the murder.
O'Dell's supporters say DNA testing proves he did not carry out the crime.
